question: In 2025, what share of orders contained more than one item line? Compare average ordered units per order for one-line and multi-line orders; also report orders with no item line separately.

action.query:
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN i.ITEM_LINE_COUNT IS NULL THEN 'No item line'
    WHEN i.ITEM_LINE_COUNT = 1 THEN 'One item line'
    WHEN i.ITEM_LINE_COUNT > 1 THEN 'Multi item line'
  END AS order_type,
  COUNT(o.ORDER_ID) AS order_count,
  AVG(i.ITEM_QUANTITY) AS avg_ordered_units
FROM ZOMATO_DLR.CORE.FACT_ORDER o
LEFT JOIN ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_ORDER_ITEM_ROLLUP i
  ON o.ORDER_ID = i.ORDER_ID
WHERE o.ORDER_DATE >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ORDER_DATE < '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY order_type
ORDER BY 
  CASE order_type 
    WHEN 'No item line' THEN 0
    WHEN 'One item line' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Multi item line' THEN 2
    ELSE 3 END;

action.answer: In 2025, there were no orders with zero item lines. Of all orders, 1,307,684 (about 30%) had exactly one item line, and 3,052,089 (about 70%) had more than one item line. The average ordered units per order were 1.219753 for one-line orders and 3.484769 for multi-line orders. This shows that multi-line orders not only make up the majority but also have a significantly higher average quantity of items per order.
action.reason: The query results show counts and averages for each order type. No 'No item line' orders were present in the data. Shares and averages are directly calculated from the returned values.
